svg.title: The Intermediate Value Theorem: why continuity matters
svg.desc: Left: a continuous function on the closed interval [1, 5] with f(1) = 1 and f(5) = 5. The dashed line y = 3 lies between 1 and 5, and the curve crosses it three times, at c₁, c₂ and c₃, all inside (1, 5): the theorem promises at least one. Right: a function with a jump at x = 3 that also has f(1) = 1 and f(5) = 5 but skips over y = 3, so no c gives f(c) = 3. Without continuity the conclusion can fail.
svg.text: Continuous on [1, 5]: at least one c
A jump: the value 3 is skipped
Continuous on [a, b] and d between f(a) and f(b) ⇒ f(c) = d for some c in (a, b).
